title: Ephemeral Cache Preservation & Operator Rollback Runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic runbook for preserving ephemeral (in-memory/KV) caches during control-plane and runtime upgrades for private appliance/VPC deployments, plus a safe operator rollback path if the new controller causes regressions. Focus is on minimal disruption for customer workloads that rely on prefix/KV caches (session affinity, embedding caches, routing caches).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments (appliance or VPC-hosted control plane).
- Targeted for upgrades that change runtime binary, operator/controller, or API surface that touches cache eviction/serialization semantics.
- Assumes customers run Redwood runtime with local KV caches persisted in ephemeral tmpfs or pod-local disk (not external Redis).
- Does NOT cover migrations to external durable cache (separate playbook).

Risk model and failure modes we care about:
- Cold-cache storm after upgrade (latency spike / traffic amplification).
- Incompatible cache serialization format causing deserialization errors -> fail-open vs fail-closed decision points.
- Operator upgrade introduces a leader-election change that causes short control-plane flaps.
- Terraform provider changes accidentally recreate stateful sets / volumes.

Pre-upgrade checklist (operator/controller + runtime):
1) Confirm API compatibility matrix for target versions (see Testing matrix below).
2) Quiesce non-critical background jobs (eviction sweeps, async reindexing).
3) Snapshot pod spec and PVC bindings: kubectl get sts, pvcs, pv -o yaml -> store in artifact storage.
4) Dump runtime KV index stats: admin/metrics endpoint /admin/cache/stats -> save timestamped JSON.
5) Ensure terraform state locked and backup created (terraform state pull -> store in S3/secure location).
6) Verify monitoring alert thresholds are tuned for upgrade window (token-rate, p95 latency, error-rate).

KV cache preservation strategies (choose per customer constraints):
A) In-place graceful operator upgrade (best for short tests):
   - Operator rollout with maxUnavailable: 1 and pause-on-failure.
   - Operator should coordinate pod drains with preStop hooks that flush in-memory caches to local durable file (if enabled).
   - Pre-upgrade hook: enable cache-serialize=on (feature flag) on control-plane for 10 minutes to persist hot prefixes.

B) Transparent prefix handoff (preferred when there are multiple replicas):
   - Enable proxy-layer sticky routing to seed warmed caches (traffic weighting 80/20 to canaries).
   - Run warmup traffic generator for top 100 paths for 15 minutes post-upgrade.

C) Snapshot-and-restore (when acceptable to pause writes briefly):
   - Trigger /admin/cache/snapshot -> produces tarball under /var/tmp/cache-snap-<ts>.tar.gz.
   - rsync snapshot to new node or to stable NFS mount accessible to new runtime instance.
   - On new runtime start, set env CACHE_RESTORE_PATH to snapshot location and pass flag --restore-cache.

Terraform module notes (practical tips):
- Pin provider versions in module root to prevent surprise tf provider bumps during planned upgrades. Example: required_providers { kubernetes = { version = "~> 2.9" } }
- For stateful resources (sts, pvcs), add lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } to avoid accidental replacement during plan apply.
- Use terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan and store the plan artifact in the release bundle for audit.
- If adding new fields to module inputs (e.g., cache_persistence_enabled), follow two-step rollout: 1) accept new input with default null, 2) re-deploy with explicit true in later patch.
- When migrating TF module versions: run tf state list | grep module.<name> to validate resource address stability.

API compatibility shim checklist:
- If the new operator introduces a change in /v1/admin/cache endpoints, provide a compatibility shim that translates old payloads to the new JSON schema for 30 days.
- Add integration tests in CI that run both old and new client versions against a compatibility-proxy container.
- Define clear deprecation headers and client-side warnings: X-Redwood-Cache-Compat: deprecated-v1 -> include in responses for 30 days.

Canary and rollout strategy (practical steps):
1) Deploy new operator/controller to a single control-plane zone or single-appliance first.
2) Shadow-traffic mode for 30 minutes: route 10% of requests to canary while responses are ignored by client (compare metrics).
3) Move to weighted traffic 50%/50% for 10–30 minutes if metrics stable.
4) Ramp to 100% and then watch p95/p99 and error spikes for 15 minutes before marking finished.

Automated checks during warmup and canary:
- Cache hit-rate for top prefixes should not drop by >10% vs baseline.
- Response time p95 should not increase by >20% over baseline.
- Error rate > 0.5% -> auto pause rollout and start rollback.

Rollback playbook (fastest safe path):
- Trigger: observed metrics breach or deserialization errors in logs.
- High-level: revert operator to previous image tag, re-apply terraform if plan created any drift, and coordinate cache restore if snapshot path was used.
- Immediate steps: 
  1) kubectl rollout undo deploy/redwood-operator -n redwood || kubectl set image deploy/redwood-operator redwood-operator=registry.redwood/release:<prev-tag>
  2) If rolling back operator does not restore control-plane behavior within 2 minutes, scale down new runtime pods gradually: kubectl scale sts/runtime --replicas=0 then bring back previous version from saved image.
  3) If snapshot was used, set CACHE_RESTORE_PATH and restart runtime pods with --force-restore flag.
  4) Post-rollback: run consistency check: /admin/cache/integrity-check -> expect no more than 0.1% of keys flagged for manual reconciliation.

Observability & telemetry gating:
- Create ephemeral alert channel for the upgrade (pagerduty rotation + slack #upgrade-watch).
- Add metric tags upgrade.window=<id>, upgrade.phase={canary, ramp, finalize, rollback} to make event correlation easy.
- Temporarily raise alert thresholds for certain flapping metrics to avoid noise; track raw counts separately.

Customer communication snippets (use in CS comms):
- Pre-upgrade: "Planned control-plane maintenance on <date/time>. We expect short-lived increases in latency while caches warm; no data loss expected. Contact: cs@redwood.com."
- Post-rollback: "We observed an unexpected cache serialization error and rolled back to the previous version; customers affected may see transient increased latency. Incident: JIRA-DEPLOY-982."

Testing matrix (must pass before wide rollout):
- Client versions: 1.2.x, 1.3.x, 1.4.x
- Operator versions: current (v2024.12.1) -> target (v2025.01.0)
- Runtime variants: small-seq (intel-rt-1), gpu-rt (nvidia-quant), cpu-rt (x86-compact)
- Required tests: endpoint smoke, /admin/cache/snapshot & restore, key-format roundtrip test, canary traffic comparison, terraform apply dry-run validation

Post-upgrade validation (15m, 1h, 24h):
- 15m: basic health (k8s probe, control-plane leader present), cache hit rate back to within 90% of baseline, no deserialization errors in logs.
- 1h: traffic fully ramped, p99 within SLO, no manual operator interventions.
- 24h: run extended consistency job and confirm cache integrity check % < 0.05%.

Playbook snippets / commands (examples):
- Snapshot: curl -s -X POST http://<runtime-host>/admin/cache/snapshot -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -o cache-snap-$(date +%s).json
- Restore: kubectl set env sts/runtime CACHE_RESTORE_PATH=/mnt/snap/cache-snap-<ts>.json && kubectl rollout restart sts/runtime
- Operator rollback: kubectl rollout undo deploy/redwood-operator -n redwood || kubectl set image deploy/redwood-operator redwood-operator=registry.redwood/release:<prev-tag>
- TF plan artifact: terraform plan -out=upgrade-operator.plan && aws s3 cp upgrade-operator.plan s3://redwood-release-artifacts/<id>/

Runbook ownership and escalation:
- Primary run owner: eng-private-deployments oncall (rotate weekly).
- Escalation: if rollback takes >30 minutes or customers report >5% of requests failing, escalate to the SRE oncall + product owner.

Open action items before GA rollout:
- [ ] Implement cache-serialize preStop hook in runtime (PR: GH-PR-4521).
- [ ] Add integration test that runs restore flow in CI (CONFLUENCE-PRIV-238).
- [ ] Add terraform lifecycle prevent_destroy to sts resources in module (JIRA-DEPLOY-982).
- [ ] Author customer-facing maintenance advisory template in CS repo.

Notes and rationale (informal):
- Preserving ephemeral caches is not always worth the complexity for small customers; offer an optional toggle and default to warmup traffic for small deployments.
- Terraform conservative approach (prevent_destroy + pinned providers) reduces blast radius of accidental upgrades.
- Prefer operator-side graceful serialization over heavy-handed snapshot/restore because it's lower-latency and avoids coordination with external storage.

Appendix: quick links and snippets:
- Snapshot endpoint spec (internal): /docs/internal/admin-cache-snapshot.md (internal link)
- TF module: modules/private/runtime/sts/main.tf (module note)
